articles.title: Implant size distribution and mid-term outcomes of transfibular total ankle arthroplasty in a Japanese cohort.
articles.authors: Yano K, Ikari K, Koseki T, Tominaga A, Okazaki K
articles.population: Japanese patients with end-stage ankle arthritis undergoing transfibular total ankle arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Implant size distribution, clinical outcomes measured by SAFE-Q questionnaire and ankle range of motion, radiological alignment parameters, complications, and implant survival rate
articles.take_home: Ankle replacement surgery using the transfibular approach worked well in Japanese patients over three to four years of follow-up, with 95-98% of implants still functioning properly. Smaller implant sizes were sufficient for Japanese patients' bone structure, and function and pain improved significantly after surgery.

articles.title: Perioperative Factors Associated With Postoperative Failure-Free Survival After Arthrodesis for Diabetic Charcot Neuroarthropathy of the Foot or Ankle.
articles.authors: Wang Q, Zhang Y, Shen S, Wang J, Wang JH, Zhao HM
articles.population: Patients with Eichenholtz stage III diabetic Charcot neuroarthropathy of the foot or ankle treated with arthrodesis
articles.outcomes: Postoperative failure-free survival at 6 months and 12 months; associations with diabetes duration, smoking, and glycaemic markers
articles.take_home: After foot or ankle fusion surgery for diabetic Charcot neuroarthropathy, patients with longer diabetes duration and those who smoke had worse outcomes. About 6 in 10 patients remained stable at 12 months, but the findings need confirmation in larger studies.

articles.title: Preoperative Anxiety and/or Depression as a Predictor of Patient‑Reported Outcomes After Total Ankle Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Sundet M, Lund Eriksen M, Storronning I, Jevnaker A, Husby I, Osterhus I, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using prospectively collected registry data
articles.sample_size: 300 patients (90 with preoperative anxiety and/or depression)
articles.outcomes: Manchester-Oxford Foot and Ankle Questionnaire score at 12 months after surgery; self-reported anxiety and depression at 12 months
articles.take_home: Patients who reported anxiety or depression before ankle replacement surgery started with worse pain and function, but improved just as much as those without these symptoms over the year after surgery. About two-thirds of patients who had anxiety or depression before surgery no longer reported it a year later.

articles.title: Factors associated with surgical site infection after ankle fracture fixation: a retrospective study in northern Sweden.
articles.authors: Topalhafizoglu S, Stralmark J, Lundqvist R, Wanman J, Pietz G
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years and over undergoing ankle fracture surgery at two trauma centres in northern Sweden
articles.outcomes: Incidence of surgical site infection within 30 days of surgery or up to 1 year with an implant present; factors associated with infection risk
articles.take_home: Surgical site infections occurred in 11% of patients after ankle fracture surgery. Smoking, previous external fixation, and longer operative time were associated with higher infection risk, suggesting that quitting smoking before surgery and reducing operation time may help prevent infections.

articles.title: Outcomes of Ankle Fractures in Patients With Solid Organ Transplant.
articles.authors: Yetter TR, Aflatooni JO, Miller RR, Hernandez KL, Ahuero JS
articles.population: Patients with solid organ transplant (SOT) and matched non-SOT controls undergoing surgery for ankle fractures
articles.outcomes: 90-day emergency department visits, readmission rates, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, overall complications, nonunion or delayed union, and need for external fixation
articles.take_home: Solid organ transplant patients had similar rates of readmission, emergency department visits and overall complications to non-transplant patients after ankle fracture surgery, but they experienced higher rates of delayed bone healing and were more likely to need external fixation before definitive surgery. Closer monitoring of bone healing in transplant patients may be beneficial.

articles.title: The 50 most-cited articles on Lisfranc injuries: A bibliometric analysis.
articles.authors: Micicoi L, Grun W, Piclet-Legre B, Pozzessere E, de Cesar Netto C, Gonzalez JF
articles.sample_size: 50 most-cited articles identified from top 100 records
articles.outcomes: Citation counts, publication dates, journal sources, evidence levels, and geographical distribution of Lisfranc injury research
articles.take_home: Most research on Lisfranc injuries is low-quality evidence, with 80% being Level IV-V studies. Researchers and clinicians need better quality trials to settle disagreements about the best surgical treatments for these injuries.

articles.title: Screening for Low Bone Mineral Density Using Opportunistic Foot Radiographs.
articles.authors: Albright JA, Feldman MW, Martin T, Baker JD, Gunther R, Anderson PA, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 50 years and older who had both a foot radiograph and DXA scan within 1 year
articles.outcomes: Fifth metatarsal index measurement on foot X-rays compared with DXA scan results for osteoporosis detection; optimal cutoff of 46.8% showed 93.3% sensitivity and 95.0% specificity
articles.take_home: A simple measurement from routine foot X-rays may help identify patients with low bone density and osteoporosis, potentially offering a low-cost screening alternative to specialised bone density scans. This could help more patients get checked early for bone health problems.

articles.title: Total ankle arthroplasty via lateral transfibular approach with and without concomitant subtalar arthrodesis : radiological alignment, patient-reported outcomes, and range of motion at >/= five-year follow-up.
articles.authors: Constantinescu SA, Barbero A, Carfi C, Crippa Orlandi N, Bonzano C, Indino C, et al.
articles.population: Patients with ankle osteoarthritis, some with additional subtalar joint osteoarthritis, undergoing total ankle arthroplasty via lateral transfibular approach
articles.sample_size: 119 patients (50 with concomitant subtalar arthrodesis, 69 with isolated ankle replacement)
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcomes (pain, function, quality of life), ankle range of motion, radiological alignment, and complication rates at five or more years follow-up
articles.take_home: Patients who had both ankle and subtalar joint surgery achieved similar improvements in pain, function, and quality of life compared to those who had ankle surgery alone. Both groups improved significantly over five years, suggesting combined surgery is safe when needed.

articles.title: Poor mental health in patients with symptomatic osteochondral lesions of the talus.
articles.authors: Pijnacker JHM, Agyeman-Prempeh NO, Sierevelt IN, Emanuel KS, Broekman B, Kerkhoffs GMMJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients with symptomatic osteochondral lesions of the talus prior to treatment
articles.outcomes: Mental health assessed using Mental Health Inventory-5 (MHI-5); comparison with general Dutch population and individuals with mood or anxiety disorders; factors associated with mental health scores
articles.take_home: Patients with ankle osteochondral lesions have significantly worse mental health than the general population, with scores similar to people with diagnosed mood or anxiety disorders. Even after successful orthopaedic treatment, mental health remained poor, suggesting the need to address mental wellbeing alongside physical treatment.

articles.title: COFAS Grade is not Associated with Outcomes following Infinity Total Ankle Arthroplasty: A Multicenter Study with Minimum Five-Year Follow-Up.
articles.authors: Townshend D, Martin R, Bing A, Blundell C, Clough T, Davenport J, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total ankle replacement (Infinity fixed-bearing design) across 11 UK centres
articles.outcomes: Implant survival at 5 years, revision rates, reoperation rates, radiographic findings, patient-reported outcomes (Manchester-Oxford Foot Questionnaire, Ankle Osteoarthritis Scale, EuroQol 5-dimension)
articles.take_home: The severity of ankle arthritis and deformity did not affect how well patients did after total ankle replacement, with 98.2% of implants surviving at 5 years and patient symptoms improving significantly regardless of how complex their arthritis was beforehand.

articles.title: Low Symptom Burden, Limited Gain: Preoperative MOxFQ Predicts Outcome After Chevron Osteotomy.
articles.authors: Hamre ME, Raeder BW, Molund M
articles.population: Patients undergoing Chevron osteotomy for hallux valgus
articles.outcomes: Clinically meaningful improvement in Manchester-Oxford Foot Questionnaire score at 1 year (defined as 15-point or greater improvement)
articles.take_home: Patients with higher symptom burden before surgery were more likely to achieve meaningful improvement after Chevron osteotomy, whilst those starting with low symptoms showed limited gains. A preoperative symptom score of around 42 or higher may help identify patients most likely to benefit from surgery.

articles.title: Platelet-Rich Plasma vs Corticosteroid Injection for Morton Neuroma: A Prospective Unblinded Randomized Comparative Study.
articles.authors: Genuth G, Stavrou P, Brown C, Iselin LD
articles.population: Patients with clinically and MRI-confirmed Morton neuroma who had failed at least 6 months of conservative treatment
articles.outcomes: PROMIS Physical Function and Pain Interference scores at 3, 6, and 12 months; neuroma size on MRI at 6 months; complications
articles.take_home: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injections produced better pain relief and improved physical function than corticosteroid injections at 12 months, and also resulted in smaller neuroma size on imaging. Both treatments were generally safe, though the authors note these findings need confirmation in larger, more rigorous studies.

articles.title: Sesamoid Subluxation in Hallux Valgus Deformity.
articles.authors: Lama JE, Thompson R, Streeter SR, Jones A, Steineman BD, Ellis SJ, et al.
articles.population: Adults with and without hallux valgus (bunion)
articles.outcomes: Distance from lateral sesamoid to second metatarsal head, hallux valgus angle, intermetatarsal angle, first metatarsal pronation, and sesamoid position
articles.take_home: In patients with bunions, a key ligament in the foot stretches more than normal, allowing the sesamoid bones to move out of their usual position rather than staying anchored as previously thought. This finding suggests surgeons should avoid cutting this ligament during bunion operations.

articles.title: Revision of failed total ankle arthroplasty to a transfibular trabecular metal prosthesis.
articles.authors: Day J, Schafer KA, Choi DS, Convery K, Zhang Z, Schon LC
articles.population: Patients with failed total ankle replacement requiring revision surgery
articles.sample_size: 11 ankles in 11 patients, average age 72.1 years
articles.outcomes: Pain scores improved significantly on VAS and ankle outcome scores; ankle alignment within normal limits; 1 revision and 4 reoperations at minimum 2 years follow-up; all 4 infected cases successfully treated with two-stage revision
articles.take_home: Revision ankle replacement using this newer implant and approach improved pain and achieved good alignment in patients whose first ankle replacement had failed. This may offer an alternative to ankle fusion for selected patients wanting to avoid that operation.
